t: You're looking at the war memorial in St John's churchyard, in Hampstead. It was designed by Temple Lushington Moore, an English architect who practised in London, though his work spreads across England, especially the North. He's best known for a series of fine Gothic Revival churches built between about 1890 and 1917, and he also restored many churches and designed church fittings. Memorial crosses were another part of his work, so a memorial like this one sits comfortably within his career.
